title: TAUS: Token-Adjusted Urgency Score + OKR Heatmap for Capacity-Aware Prioritization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Proposal for a new prioritization framework that augments RICE-style scoring with explicit token-cost and latency-capacity signals and ties each initiative to OKR heatmap bands. The Token-Adjusted Urgency Score (TAUS) is intended to help roadmap decisions where per-token economics, model latency profiles, and Dedicated/Private capacity constraints materially change the benefit/cost calculus. This doc includes: 1) TAUS formula and component definitions, 2) OKR heatmap mapping guidance, 3) capacity-aware adjustment rules (Dedicated vs Hosted), 4) guidance for PM/Eng tradeoffs and rollout plan, and 5) telemetry & dashboards required for operationalizing the score.
acceptance_criteria: TAUS formula documented with examples for text-generation and embedding workloads
OKR heatmap mapping defined (Objective alignment bands and threshold values)
Capacity adjustment rules created that flag high-cost/latency items for Dedicated-only or deferred rollout
Prototype scoring implemented in a spreadsheet and linked to the product roadmap view
Telemetry requirements captured: per-route token distribution, median/95p latency, cost-per-token, model-variant availability
Stakeholder sign-off from Eng (runtime), Data (cost metrics), and GTM (OKR owners)

formula_summary: TAUS = (ImpactScore * Reach) / (TokenCostAdjusted + LatencyPenalty) * OKRAlignmentMultiplier. Where TokenCostAdjusted = AvgTokensPerRequest * CostPerToken * TokenWeightingFactor. LatencyPenalty = max(0, (p95_latency_ms - latency_target_ms) / latency_target_ms) * LatencySensitivity. OKRAlignmentMultiplier in {0.8,1.0,1.2} based on Low/Medium/High alignment.
tradeoffs_and_notes: We intentionally keep TAUS multiplicative to preserve strong signals from OKR alignment; small changes in multiplier can reorder close-scoring initiatives.
TokenCost should use long-run amortized cost (including KV cache savings and batching) rather than short-term spot GPU rates to avoid over-penalizing experiments.
LatencyPenalty must be applied per-customer cohort when Dedicated/Private capacity differences exist; single global latency number hides important variance.
We recommend a guardrail: do not let TAUS alone veto strategic bets (add a 'strategic enabling' tag for forced consideration).
